articles.title: Mikel Arteta furious with Sunderland 'judo roll' penalty vs Arsenal: 'No penalty in any game, any league'
articles.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta saw his side produce plenty and let the spoils mostly go to waste on Saturday in a 2-0 win over Sunderland, but his mind was only o...
articles.body:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta saw his side produce plenty and let the spoils mostly go to waste on Saturday in a 2-0 win over Sunderland , making goalkeeper David Raya the hero of the day.

But he was left angry with the fact that Raya had to save a penalty in the first place, as Arteta felt Daniel Ballard used a 'judo roll' to win a penalty off Ezri Konsa as Arsenal were penalized for physical play in the box.

"I'm so upset — it's unacceptable at this level," Arteta said. "It can change a season, a championship. I watched it 10 times. It's a judo roll. It just cannot happen."

Arteta was shown a yellow card in the first half for drifting into the Sunderland technical area, so he was already on edge well before forcing the penalty narrative into his postgame interview.

"It's a huge win but it could've been something very different," Arteta said. "They could've changed the game."

Bruno Guimaraes came off the bench and slammed the Gunners in front, moments after Sunderland saw a penalty saved by Raya, and Guimaraes was asked whether Raya was the best keeper in the world.

"Definitely," Guimaraes said. "Very good saves. He keeps us alive in the game, that unbelievable moment saving the penalty. I think after this moment we got a big confidence to play forward and score our goal. He's an unbelievable player."

The Spanish keeper would later make three interventions including two saves in a wild scrum during the 84th minute.

The Gunners would earn a penalty deep in stoppage time to give the game its final score line, and Saka snapped it past Robin Roefs .

Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka alone had multiple brilliant chances for Arsenal but the Black Cats were either let off the hook or stepped up to put out the fires at the Stadium of Light.

Mikel Arteta reaction after Arsenal escapes another tight game with a 2-0 win

Arteta attempted to get the postmatch interviewer to mention the penalty kick, finishing his first answer with, "They could've changed the game."

When asked about what could've changed the game, Arteta acted bewildered that the reporter didn't immediately know.

When she hazarded a guess that it was Sunderland being awarded a penalty, he went off with the aforementioned quote about Ballard doing a judo roll on Konsa. Ballard had a piece of Konsa's sleeve but seemed already headed to ground.

"It's not a penalty in any game, in any case, in any contest, in any league."

Arteta would go on to praise his players for their role in picking up all three points under that pressure.

"It's unbelievable the playershave with the courage to go again and again and again," Arteta said. "I'm so pleased in one sense and so worried in another."

Arteta would go on to say he's worried because his team should've never conceded a penalty in that manner.

But he knows he has a special keeper in Raya.

"Unbelievable. Again, he's a player that decides football matches when we need it. Big credit to Sunderland the way they play and the way they are coached. They deserve a lot of credit for the way they make you work."

articles.title: Social media reacts to Oklahoma's 17-10 loss to Michigan
articles.summary: The Oklahoma Sooners suffered a disappointing loss to the Michigan Wolverines and here's how social media reacted.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners suffered one of the more disappointing losses of the Brent Venables era in their 17-10 loss to the Michigan Wolverines . The Oklahoma defense did enough, but the offense couldn't find any consistency behind a rough performance from John Mateer.

The Sooners entered the game as road favorites but struggled to establish an identity on the offensive side of the ball. Even though they found success with Lloyd Avant early in the game, he only received five first-half carries and four in the second half.

The playcalling was questionable and so was John Mateer's performance. He only completed 52% of his passes and was off-target on a number of throws in the fourth quarter. He'll be under the microscope along with Arbuckle moving forward.

There are going to be a lot of questions about what Oklahoma's doing on offense after a letdown in what was a winnable game for the Sooners. But here's how social media reacted to the Sooners' loss to Michigan.

articles.title: South Dakota football rolls past Eastern Washington, moves to 3-0
articles.summary: South Dakota outscored Eastern Washington 24-10 in the middle two quarters to beat the Eagles and move to 3-0 on the season.
articles.body:
South Dakota ripped off 21 consecutive points between the second and third quarters to turn a 10-3 lead into a 31-3 advantage, and the Coyotes finished off a 41-23 win over Eastern Washington on Saturday, Sept. 12, in the DakotaDome.

The Coyotes scored all three touchdowns during that run on long plays. Austyn Modrzewski hit Tennell Bryant for a 66-yard touchdown, then Charles Pierre Jr. ripped off a 72-yard touchdown run. Modrzewski and Bryant connected again for a 48-yard passing score.

Eastern Washington scored touchdowns for three of the final five scores of the game to make the final margin closer.

See the best moments of South Dakota football preseason practice

Modrzewski finished 16-for-24 for 245 yards and three touchdowns passing, but he did throw his first collegiate interception on a pass to the end zone. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.

Bryant had three catches for 120 yards and the two scores, Brayden White contributed four catches for 34 yards and a touchdown, Tysen Boze hauled in two passes for 44 yards, Pierre had a 21-yard grab and Keyondray Jones-Logan had three receptions for 17 yards.

Pierre had his biggest day of the season on the ground, running for 138 yards and two scores on 15 totes. Jones-Logan had 49 yards on eight rushes, Jackson Proctor ran it five times for 50 yards and Carson Fletcher had five carries for 18 yards.

Nate Laperi led the Coyote defense with two sacks, while Chris Dixon , Asher Tomaszewski and Tyler Sapit all recorded one each. Ethan Carrier picked a pass off and ran it back 44 yards, and Gabriel Hardman had two tackles for a loss and a forced fumble.

The Coyotes are now 3-0 and will travel to FBS Boise State on Saturday, Sept. 19.

articles.title: Fever news: Fans are fed up with Caitlin Clark's lack of Team USA playing time
articles.summary: Team USA defeated Team Spain 76-66 in their FIBA World Cup game on Saturday. Once again, Caitlin Clark, a 2026 WNBA MVP candidate, did not start the game. C...
articles.body:
Team USA defeated Team Spain 76-66 in their FIBA World Cup game on Saturday. Once again, Caitlin Clark , a 2026 WNBA MVP candidate, did not start the game. Clark's playing time has been a subject of discussion throughout the tournament. Many fans and even some media members were especially fed up after Clark saw just under 17 minutes of playing time on Saturday.

"Team USA's 10-point win over Spain was closer than it needed to be. That's because Caitlin Clark , the WNBA's best player, should start, orchestrate and be featured more," Skip Bayless wrote on X, formerly Twitter. "But of course, Kara Lawson can't risk a mutiny of veterans. This is all so petty, so dumb, so hard to watch."

"Today's game is clear evidence that there's an agenda being pushed with Caitlin Clark," a fan added . "Why the h*ll is she barely playing? She's been one of the best players on this team. At this point, it feels like they're doing everything they can to limit her impact and make her look bad."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

BricksCenter, an account on X, called out Clark's Team USA teammates for "icing" her out.

One fan specifically called out Jackie Young .

"I legit think Jackie Young would rather throw the ball to a fan in the crowd than Caitlin Clark… She just looked her off wide open to throw a spinning no look to Stewie that only wasn't a turnover because Stewie has a 7 foot wingspan," the post reads .

Clark has not played especially well while on the floor during the FIBA World Cup. She went 0-3 from the field on Saturday and recorded only one point via a free throw. She is averaging 7.0 points per outing on 29.4 percent shooting from the field and 22.7 percent shooting from beyond the arc for the tournament. Her playing time has been up and down, as Clark is averaging 20 overall minutes per contest.

Clark's +110 plus-minus leads Team USA's roster, however. She is clearly still making an impact despite her underwhelming scoring numbers. Clark has been able to find her teammates while on the floor, averaging 5.8 assists per game.

Clark Report also shared an intriguing statistic about Clark and Aliyah Boston .

In all reality, Caitlin Clark could be starting and it would help Team USA. However, the team seems to be relying on its veterans. Still, Clark's impact has been significant while on the floor.

articles.title: Who won halftime between Alabama State and Troy? Battle of the bands
articles.summary: Battle of the Bands: Who won halftime showdown between Alabama State's Mighty Marching Hornets and Troy's Sound of the South.
articles.body:
TROY — It wasn't the best showing for Alabama State football in the first half against Troy, but luckily, the Mighty Marching Hornets had a chance to inject some life into the Alabama State faithful .

In a rare FCS and FBS battle of the bands, the Mighty Marching Hornets went toe-to-toe with Troy's Sound of the South during the halftime of Alabama State and Troy's game on Saturday, Sept. 12.

It was battle of different styles, an HBCU band against a more traditional college band, but who claimed the halftime show? See what the Montgomery Advertiser observed during halftime.

This might've been the closest category when it came to the two performances, but what the Sound of the South did to win this category was its ability to switch up the beat, the sound level and how quickly it could make an impact when needed.

It's hard to compete with drum majors who not only make sure the band stays on rhythm, but partake in the dancing on the field. This one goes to the Mighty Marching Hornets because, again, performances are about bringing the energy.

The Stingettes are hard to match on any given day because of the energy they bring to the performance. The Stingettes do flips and synchronized dances, adding to the performance.

It's hard to pick against the Sound of the South in this category. It's performance had a solid variety of different beloved songs from beloved Disney movies and music icons like Queen. It was a nice touch at the end of the performance to mix in traditional college sounds.

This was a close one to pick, the Sound of the South's variety of song choices was intriguing, but it felt more like something to be admired. The Mighty Marching Hornets performance made one want to get up and dance.

articles.title: Missed chances in home defeat
articles.summary: RBS women lose to Altach FC Red Bull Salzburg Women 1-3 SCR Altach (H/T:0-3). Goals: Grünwald (75.) - Mikulica (12., 45., 45.+2)SCR Altach secured a 3–1 win...
articles.body:
FC Red Bull Salzburg Women 1-3 SCR Altach (H/T:0-3). Goals: Grünwald (75.) - Mikulica (12., 45., 45.+2)

SCR Altach secured a 3–1 win at Liefering's Saalachspitz with some clinical counter-attacking. While Dusan Pavlovic's squad dictated the tempo of this ADMIRAL Women's Bundesliga match, the visitors were far more ruthless in front of goal. Hat-trick hero Mikulica effectively won the encounter herself.

Our team took to the pitch aiming to follow up on the previous week's emphatic cup win with a strong league performance. Katja Wienerroither threatened early on with a header, while Magdalena Schwarz and Alessia Pamminger also underlined the promising start with initial attempts. However, it was the visitors who found the net first. After a long ball forward from Lüscher, Mikulica suddenly broke clear - making it 1-0 (12').

Essentially, the story of the first 45 minutes was that we controlled the game, but Altach scored the goals. Lena Triendl tested goalkeeper Busse, while our captain Wienerroither failed to convert a prime opportunity set up by Triendl shortly afterwards. At the other end, Baumgartner and Mikulica launched a counter-attack and the latter finished inside the far corner (45') - and did so again two minutes later, completing a perfect hat-trick after a clever turn (45+2'). The teams headed into the break with the scoreline a disappointing 0–3.

Giving up wasn't an option. Substitute Christina Gierzinger set the tone as her shot from 20 yards out came very close to sparking a comeback. Emelie Kobler, also coming off the bench, was on the end of a neat passing sequence, though the finishing touch was still lacking . Then Valentina Lutz won the ball on the flank and played it to Julia Grünwald who drove past the defenders and found the net via the inside of the post, offering a glimmer of hope as we pulled it back to 1-3 (75').

We kept pushing, repeatedly putting the visitors under pressure in the closing stages. However, there were no further celebrations to be had. Ultimately, our team suffered their first home defeat of the season.

We conceded three goals from counter-attacks simply because we didn't defend well. Altach have the quality to finish those chances off. It felt like we were the ones dictating play in the first half, yet they were the ones scoring the goals. After the break, we reacted better to losing possession and created chances -though unfortunately, we only managed to score once. It wasn't all negative as we haven't had this many opportunities in a long time. It's just tough that we were punished for every mistake. Now we have to accept this and do better next time.

articles.summary: Josh Kerr, Jakob Ingebrigtsen, Amy Hunt and Keely Hodgkinson are all set to star in Budapest to conclude the 2026 outdoor season
articles.body:
The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships begin in Budapest across three action-packed days as some of the sport's biggest names battle.

The new competition, which will bring the top level 2026 track season to a close, sees most top stars face off across three days of action in the Hungarian capital and there is significant prize money up for grabs.

On Friday's opening night of action, Jakob Ingebrigtsen stormed to a stunning win in the 5000m – but the Norwegian has since withdrawn from a 1500m showdown with Josh Kerr and Cole Hocker. Audrey Werro, meanwhile, proved imperious again as she got the better of Keely Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol in the 800m.

Here is everything you need to know about the competition.

What is the World Athletics Ultimate Championships?

It is a new concept intended to fill the void in non-Olympic or World Championship years, designed to pit the biggest names against each other for what World Athletics have said is the biggest prize pot in track and field.

The idea is to make it fast-paced and action-packed to keep viewers engaged.

Two semi-finals in the 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 100m hurdles/110m hurdles and 400m hurdles will feature eight athletes and the top four in each will make it through to the final. The 1500m, 5000m and relays will be straight finals.

All field events will be straight finals. World Athletics say that the horizontal jumps and throws will feature four rounds, with each of the eight athletes guaranteed two attempts.

The event will be spread across three days at Budapest's National Athletics Centre and will run from Friday 11 September Sunday 13 with three-hour sessions each evening.

World Athletics Ultimate Championships schedule

For fans in the UK, all three days will be shown live by the BBC, with Sunday night's session on BBC One. It will also be available to stream on iPlayer.

World Athletics are promising a record prize pot of $10m (£7.3m) for the entire championships with top prizes of $150,000 (£110,000) for the winners of the individual events.

articles.title: Dante Moore and the Oregon Ducks fall 39-31 to Oklahoma State
articles.summary: UCLA saw a Big Ten Conference rival unexpectedly lose on Saturday, with the Oregon Ducks falling to the Oklahoma State Cowboys.
articles.body:
Before the UCLA Bruins kicked off on Saturday for their Week 2 matchup versus San Diego State , the team had seen a fellow Big Ten Conference team drop a shocker. No. 6 Oregon fell on the road to Drew Mestemaker and the Oklahoma State Cowboys .

Oregon had a chance late but would ultimately fall 39-31. Former UCLA quarterback Dante Moore had a chance to tie the game late in the fourth quarter but Ducks running back Dierre Hill Jr. fumbled a handoff which was recovered by the Cowboys to seal the game.

Moore, one of the projected top picks in the NFL Draft, struggled against Oklahoma State . Moore completed less than half of his passes, going 14/29 through the air for 191 yards and a pair of passing touchdowns.

Ducks Wire writer Dan Smalley wrote about Oregon's shortcomings on Saturday.

"With the loss, Oregon drops to 1-1 on the season, but their ranking and national championship aspirations took a significant blow. The Ducks didn't win any phase of this game. Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker outplayed his counterpart Dante Moore . It was Mestemaker making all the plays. It was Mestemaker who made the big throws. It was Mestemaker who led his team on a scoring drive that was ultimately the difference in the game." Smalley wrote. "Not Oregon's Heisman hopeful."

UCLA and Oregon will square off in less than a month, when the Bruins head to Autzen Stadium on October 10th. Oregon went into the 2026 season with national championship aspirations but it's been tough sledding through two weeks. The Ducks held off Boise State 34-27 in Week 1 before the surprising loss on Saturday.

Oklahoma State entered the game having lost 12-straight games but the team was able to put a stop to their losing ways by upsetting Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks .

articles.title: USA edge Spain to book Women’s Basketball World Cup final against France
articles.summary: USA emerged 76-66 winners in a tense semifinal after Gabby Williams-led France powered past hosts Germany 86-64.
articles.body:
The United States will take on France in the final of the women’s basketball World Cup after scraping to a 76-66 semifinal win over Spain in Berlin.

Underdogs Spain, whose best-ever result was reaching the 2014 final against the Americans, levelled the scores at 58-all at the end of the third quarter against the defending champions on Saturday.

But the experience of the 11-time champions told in the final period as USA outscored their opponents by 10 to seal victory.

Led by 16 points from Breanna Stewart and 13 from Kahleah Copper, USA extended their winning streak at the tournament to 35 matches, a run that dates back to a semifinal defeat by Russia in 2006.

Sunday’s clash with France will be a rematch of the 2024 Paris Olympics gold medal match, which the Americans won by just one point.

“That’s over, you know what I mean? We won that game and that game is over, and this is a completely new game tomorrow,” Stewart told reporters when asked about the 2024 final.

“Everybody has their own things that continue to motivate them … but this is one game to win the gold medal in the World Cup in Berlin, and that’s our entire focus.”

It was another disappointing night, though, for Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark, who scored just one point and turned the ball over twice under intense pressure from the Spanish defence.

Spain made a fast start and built an eight-point lead midway through the first quarter.

The Americans found their rhythm and controlled much of the second and third quarters, edging ahead as Copper and Stewart kept the scoreboard ticking over.

But, as they had against Italy, the Americans allowed their intensity to drop, and Spain fought back, finishing the third quarter on a 9-2 run to draw level.

Spain had the 12,650-strong crowd behind them as a stunning upset seemed on the cards, but the Americans stood tall when it mattered, starting the final quarter with a 12-2 burst to regain control.

Gabby Williams leads France to first final

France advanced to the final for the first time after an 86-64 victory over host nation Germany earlier in the day.

Gabby Williams top scored with 22 points for the Olympic silver medallists, who preserved their unbeaten record at the tournament going into Sunday’s decider in Berlin.

The US-born Williams, who also dished out five assists and recorded four steals, was the constant threat on both ends of the floor for the French.

Admitting she was “on a mission”, Williams told BeIN Sports: “I just want to give it my all.

“You never know when you’ll get an opportunity like this. You don’t know if it’ll be the last one. So, I’m just going to give everything.”

Marieme Badiane told reporters the French would not be daunted by the prospect of trying to stop the American juggernaut.

“We all realise that we can go for the ultimate prize. That’s the goal now. We aren’t stopping here. No one is going to let up.”

Outsiders Germany swept past European champions Belgium in their quarterfinal clash for a first semifinal appearance as a unified country, with East Germany having made the final four in 1967.

France burst out of the blocks early, but the Germans stayed hot on their heels, trailing by just two at the end of the opening period.

France’s quality told as the match went on and they scored nine unanswered points to begin the second half, surging into a 16-point lead.

Alexis Peterson and Emily Bessoir hit threes in the final quarter as the Germans cut the lead to nine to stay within touch, but France pulled away again with a 12-0 run to close out the match.
